rationale: The candidate reads as a small cross-shaped or pinwheel mass rather than one clear long-span gymnasium hall. Across views the orange solids remain legible, but the geometry is fragmented in plan, with crossing wings and no dominant occupiable volume that can plausibly host a clear-span sports program. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly: there is no convincing public void, entry seam, or undercut aligned to access, so the ground condition is effectively sealed. The silhouette is not a staircase problem; it is instead a continuity and typology problem. The profiled-hall section exists, but the resulting roof does not express span, daylight, or a hall section strongly enough to satisfy the gymnasium contract. The form is internally coherent as a manifold mass, yet semantically it resembles an abstract sculptural bar/cross more than a sports hall. The counterfactual and similar references suggest a longer, calmer bar with a legible threshold and roof expression would be more appropriate.
